citeturn6academia13 [wordlim: 200] Published: 10 months ago; We show in a uniform way that Dyer's conjecture is true when using the infinite Bruhat closure (instead of Bruhat preclosure) if the join exists between two elements.
Title: Bruhat Preclosure
Authors: Aram Dermenjian
Date: Tue Dec  9 15:26:17 2025

In 2011, Dyer published a series of conjectures on the weak order of Coxeter groups. One of these conjectures stated that the inversion set of the join of two elements in a Coxeter group is equal to some "closure" of the union of their inversion sets. In this paper we show that this "closure" is in fact a preclosure, which we call the Bruhat preclosure, but is a closure whenever our underlying set is an inversion set. By performing the Bruhat preclosure an infinite number of times we obtain a closure which we call the infinite Bruhat closure. We show in a uniform way that Dyer's conjecture is true when using the infinite Bruhat closure (instead of Bruhat preclosure) if the join exists between two elements. Finally, we end by showing in type A, the Bruhat preclosure is a closure thus giving a (second) proof that Dyer's conjecture is true in type A.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Density as a graph parameter is involved in many open problems in edge-coloring. The main goal of this project is to apply density-related techniques such as a generalization of the Tashkinov tree method obtained in attacking the Goldberg-Seymour conjecture, and a generalized Kempe Change method developed in exploring the Hilton-Zhao conjecture, to attack the following density-related problems: (1) the Hilton-Zhao conjecture and the overfull conjecture; (2) Gupta's co-density conjecture; (3) Goldberg's generalization of the total coloring conjecture for multigraphs; and (4) finding efficient algorithms to color graphs with the optimal number of colors in the conjectures above. The PI is also hoping to develop new density-related techniques through exploring the above problems.

## Theses and Dissertations

# Classification and Analysis of Families of Graphs with Focus on Nordhaus-Gaddum Bounds

  * Sibi Pranav Muthuprakash, Brigham Young UniversityFollow

## Abstract

Nordhaus-Gaddum type problems focus on bounding characteristics of graph and its complement. There are certain families of graphs which yield optimal upper bounds on various Nordhaus-Gaddum characteristics of graph. In this paper, we will talk about bounding combinatorial algebraic connectivity, normalized algebraic connectivity, the Cheeger constant, and the isoperimetric number of a graph and its complement. We will identify some optimal or near optimal families of graphs and conduct an analysis on these families that will help to bound these characteristics. We will also prove and conjecture some bounds that can help in formulating stronger bounds on these characteristics of graphs.
